title: High-throughput High-content Detection of Genetic Modifiers of Neurodegeneration in Human Stem Cell Derived Neurons
protocol: Check the culture under the microscope to confirm that the neurons are viable and have the correct morphology.
Treat the culture with the caspase inhibitor z-VAD-FMK at 500 nM for 30 minutes in the incubator by adding the inhibitor directly to the culture medium.

Aspirate the culture medium from the dishes, and then add 1XDPBS into the dish to wash out the residue medium; approximately 2 ml per 35 mm Petri dish or proportional volumes for other sizes of culture surfaces.
Aspirate the DPBS and add pre-warmed Accutase to lift the cells; approximately 0.5 ml per 35 mm Petri dish or proportional volumes for other sizes of culture surfaces.
Put the dishes into the 37°C tissue culture incubator, and incubate them for approximately 15 minutes.
Check the culture under the microscope to confirm that the neurons round up and are about to detach from the dish.
If the cells have not reached this morphology, put the dishes back into the incubator and check every ~3 minutes until the cells are about to detach.
Gently scrape the neurons off the dish with a cell scraper.
Dissociate possible clumps via gentle pipetting for 3~5 times to lift neurons into single suspended cells.
Add pre-warmed culture medium A into 15 ml or 50 ml conical tubes, ensuring the volume is 9 times that of the Accutase used.
Spin the cells at 1000 rpm for 4 minutes to collect them.
Save a small aliquot for cell counting and viability measurement.
Count the cell density and viability based on Trypan-blue exclusion; ensure viability is close or above 90%.
Aspirate the medium from the conical tubes.
Resuspend the cells in freezing medium, calculating the volume so that the cell density is about 5~10 X 10^6/ml.
Aliquot the cells into cryopreservation tubes at 1 ml per vial.
Put the vials into the cell freezing container.
Keep the boxes in the -80°C freezer for one or more days.
Transfer the vials into cryopreservation boxes and store them in liquid N2 tanks.
Pre-cool the dishes in a clean, ethanol-sprayed metal tray on ice.
Pre-cool a tube of X-Vivo 10 medium on ice.
Pipette up and down the cooled X-Vivo 10 medium to cool down the 5 ml pipette tube.
Prepare 1:30 matrigel by mixing 1 volume of matrigel with 29 volumes of X-Vivo 10 medium on ice via pipetting.
Keep the diluted matrigel and the culture dishes cold.
Coat the culture dishes by adding the diluted matrigel, 2 ml per 35 mm Petri dish.
Transfer the coated dishes into the 4°C fridge to coat overnight.
Warm up the coated dishes in a 37°C incubator for ~30 minutes.
Check the dishes under microscope to confirm successful coating.
Pre-warm complete culture medium A in a 37°C bath.
Thaw cells by incubating frozen vials in a 37°C bath for ~2 minutes with gentle shaking until most content becomes liquidized.
Briefly mix the content in the vial by gentle pipetting and transfer to pre-warmed culture medium A (9 ml per thawed vial) in conical tubes.
Collect the thawed cells by spinning at 1000 rpm for 4 minutes.
Save an aliquot for measuring cell density and viability.
Count the cell density and viability based on Trypan-blue exclusion; ensure viability is close or above 70%.
Aspirate the medium and add culture medium A to resuspend cells to achieve a concentration of 1X10^6 cells/ml.
Aspirate the matrigel and plate the cells to coated culture dishes at 2 ml per 35 mm Petri dish, adjusting for different sizes of culture surfaces.
Change the medium the next day with fresh pre-warmed complete culture medium.
Check the culture to ensure that the neurons look fine.
Change culture medium with fresh ones every three days.
Dissolve purchased siRNA with OPTI-MEM to reach a concentration of 10 μM.
Add water gradually around the bottom of each well and then pipette up and down slowly with multi-channel pipettes to dissolve stamped siRNAs completely.
Spin down at >1000 rpm for 1 minute to collect all dissolved siRNAs.
Transfer 3 μl of each siRNA to each well of the 96-well clear bottom PDL-coated plates by multi-channel pipettes.
Add 1 volume of Lipofectamine RNAiMax to 9 volumes of Opti-MEM.
Mix by inverting the tubes for approximately 5 times.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Add 3 μl of Lipofectamine RNAiMax containing Opti-MEM into the siRNA in each well using multi-channel pipettes.
Mix by gentle pipetting for approximately 3 times.
Put the lids back on the plates.
Incubate the transfection mix in the hood for 30 minutes; incubation up to 1 hour is acceptable.
Lift the ESC or iPSC derived neurons via the same procedure as described in step1.3 through 1.10.
Resuspend the cell pellet with complete culture medium C to reach a concentration of 1.8～2 X 106 cells/ml.
Pipette up and down gently to mix the cells.
Add 54 μl of the cell suspension on top of the transfection mix in each well of the PDL-coated 96-well plates.
Avoid air bubbles when pipetting.
Mix the cells with the transfection mix by horizontal shaking of the plates.
Incubate the plates in a 37°C tissue culture incubator for 6 hours.
Add 180 μl of pre-warmed complete culture medium C to each well using multi-channel pipettes.
Place the plates into the IncuCyte inside the incubator.
Ensure that the underside of each plate is clean and free from dust.
Wipe the underside of the plates with a lint-free tissue moistened with 70% ethanol if necessary.
Place the plates into the IncuCyte and ensure they are fully inserted into the microplate tray holder.
Select the “Schedule Upcoming Scans” option in the IncuCyte software.
Populate the gantry view with plate information for each plate.
Choose the appropriate tray location and select Tray Type: Microplates.
Under Vessel Type, select the correct definition for the microplate used.
Select “Phase-Contrast” under “Scan Type”.
Select “Edit Scan Patterns” and create a new pattern by selecting all 96 wells and 4 fields per well for image collection.
Apply the newly created scan pattern to each plate.
Under the “Properties” tab, add an appropriate Label for the plate and provide information about the cells used.
Right-click on the “Timeline” to set a new scan interval; schedule 24 hour repeating scans every 4 to 12 hours.
Let the plates equilibrate within the IncuCyte for at least 10 minutes before commencing the first scan.
Click the “Apply” button to initiate the changes to the scan schedule, and the scan will start at the next scheduled time point after the current time.
Perform a 1:10 dilution of the NucView 488 caspase-3 dye with Opti-MEM.
Add 2 μl of diluted dye into each well 24 hours after siRNA transfection in iPSC-derived neurons.
Setup the IncuCyte software as specified for Option A i) through vi), selecting “Fluorescence and Phase-Contrast” under Scan Type.
During the assay, review high definition phase contrast images to ensure quality.
Plot kinetic “Confluence v1.5” data regularly with IncuCyte software to monitor treatment effects and determine a suitable endpoint for the assay (usually 3 to 4 days).
Export the “Confluence v1.5” data using the IncuCyte software for analysis.
If experiments require 7 days or longer, change approximately 75% of the culture medium with fresh media every 7 days.
Plot the Confluence v1.5 metric over time for each condition.
Establish threshold criteria to determine rescue effects based on modifier performance.
Review phase contrast and green channel fluorescence images 24 hours after adding the dye to ensure assay quality.
Analyze fluorescence images using the IncuCyte software’s "Object Counting v2.0 algorithm".
Choose Segmentation: Fixed Threshold and input a suitable threshold value to differentiate foreground fluorescent cells from background fluorescence.
Use the Edge Split v2.0 tool to separate adjacent objects that would otherwise be masked together.
Apply filters \(size, shape and intensity) to further refine image segmentation.
Review the fluorescence image analysis by plotting the “Object Confluence metric”.
Export the “Object Confluence” and “Confluence v1.5” metrics.
Normalize the kinetic “Object Confluence” data to the initial “Confluence v1.5” value.
Plot the bar graph of the normalized caspase-3 signals.
